newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila big banks cut prime rate, but only slightly.
newsitem.headline: Manila big banks cut prime rate, but only slightly.

text.p: Several major banks in the Philippines cut their prime lending rates on Tuesday, a day after the central bank brought down its closely-watched overnight borrowing rate by three percentage points to 22 percent.
However, the rate adjustments were less than three percentage points, treasurers and corporate bankers said.
Some banks did not change their rates due to uncertainties in the foreign exchange market.

Among the banks which cut their rates were Philippine National Bank which lowered its rate to 22.5 percent from 25 percent and Philippine Commercial International Bank which trimmed its rate to 23 percent from 24 percent on Monday.
A foreign bank, which is strong in corporate banking but declined to be named, said it cut its rate to 21 percent from Monday's 22 percent.
Far East Bank and Trust Co Inc kept its rate unchanged at 22 percent, a treasury official said.
Another major local bank, which has a strong corporate client base, said it retained its rate at 21 percent.
Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc, the country's biggest bank, declined to give its rate.
Prime rates were as high as 35 percent two weeks ago when the central bank boosted its rate to 32 percent at the height of the peso crisis.
